notes: All advertised tools are included in `snapshotTools` and passed to `createServerWithTools` without a flag or capability gate (dist/index.js:714-727, dist/index.js:729-734).

The browser-extension side of the WebSocket protocol is not included in the provided source. For tools whose effects depend on browser/page behavior, `undetermined` is true and labels are kept on the least-restrictive reading.

browser_click.rationale: `browser_click` sends the parsed `element`/`ref` target to the browser as `browser_click` and then returns an accessibility snapshot. The post-click snapshot can expose private/authenticated page content (`SECRET`) or attacker-authored page content (`UNTRUSTED`). Clicking a chosen page element can submit or trigger delivery of agent-prepared page state to the current web page/site, so it is treated as a `SINK`; `element` and `ref` identify the target. The browser extension behavior is not included, so exact event and network behavior is undetermined.

browser_get_console_logs.rationale: `browser_get_console_logs` requests `browser_get_console_logs` from the connected browser, JSON-stringifies each log, joins them, and returns the result as text. Console logs may contain private data from authenticated pages (`SECRET`) and can also be authored by attacker-controlled pages (`UNTRUSTED`). The extension-side implementation is not included, so exact log scope is undetermined.

browser_go_back.rationale: `browser_go_back` sends `browser_go_back` to the connected browser and returns `captureAriaSnapshot`, whose text contains the page URL, title, and accessibility snapshot. Browser history pages may be private/authenticated (`SECRET`) or attacker-authored web pages (`UNTRUSTED`). There is no call-time destination argument. The extension-side behavior is not present, so exact browser reach is undetermined.

browser_go_forward.rationale: `browser_go_forward` sends `browser_go_forward` to the connected browser and returns `captureAriaSnapshot`, including page URL, title, and page snapshot. Forward-history pages may contain non-public user data (`SECRET`) or attacker-controlled page text (`UNTRUSTED`). There is no call-time destination argument. The extension implementation is absent, so exact reach is undetermined.

browser_hover.rationale: `browser_hover` sends a target `element`/`ref` to the browser and returns an accessibility snapshot. The returned current page information can contain private/authenticated content (`SECRET`) or attacker-authored web content (`UNTRUSTED`). `element` and `ref` select the element affected by the hover. The extension-side implementation is absent, so exact browser/page effects are undetermined.

browser_navigate.rationale: `browser_navigate` parses an agent-supplied `url` and sends it to the connected browser over the WebSocket as `browser_navigate`, then returns `captureAriaSnapshot`. The snapshot includes page URL, title, and accessibility snapshot text, so navigating the user's browser can return authenticated/private browser content (`SECRET`) or attacker-controlled web content (`UNTRUSTED`). The `url` argument selects an agent-chosen destination and causes browser navigation/request, so it is a `SINK`. The browser extension implementation is not included, so exact URL schemes and browser reach are not settled; labels are kept on the least-restrictive reading.

browser_press_key.rationale: `browser_press_key` sends the agent-supplied `key` to the connected browser as `browser_press_key`. A focused attacker-controlled page can observe typed key input or use keys such as Enter to submit page state, so `key` is content delivered to a browser/page destination and the tool is a `SINK`. The tool only returns a local status string echoing the key, not browser page content. The extension-side implementation is absent, so exact key handling is undetermined.

browser_screenshot.rationale: `browser_screenshot` requests `browser_screenshot` from the connected browser and returns the resulting PNG image data. A screenshot of the current tab can include private/authenticated content (`SECRET`) or attacker-controlled page pixels (`UNTRUSTED`). The extension implementation is not included, so exact capture scope is undetermined.

browser_select_option.rationale: `browser_select_option` sends parsed `element`, `ref`, and `values` to the browser as `browser_select_option`, then returns an accessibility snapshot. The returned page state can contain private/authenticated content (`SECRET`) or attacker-authored content (`UNTRUSTED`). The selected `values` are agent-supplied data delivered into the current page and observable by attacker-controlled pages, so the tool is a `SINK`; `element`/`ref` select the destination control. The extension-side implementation is absent, so exact behavior is undetermined.

browser_snapshot.rationale: `browser_snapshot` returns `captureAriaSnapshot`, which gets `getUrl`, `getTitle`, and `browser_snapshot` from the connected browser and embeds them in returned text. The current page can be authenticated/private (`SECRET`) or attacker-controlled (`UNTRUSTED`). The returned snapshot can contain later-usable page URLs and element references. The extension-side implementation is not included, so exact page reach is undetermined.

browser_type.rationale: `browser_type` sends parsed `element`, `ref`, `text`, and `submit` to the browser as `browser_type`, then returns an accessibility snapshot. The snapshot can reveal private/authenticated page content (`SECRET`) or attacker-controlled page content (`UNTRUSTED`). The `text` argument is agent-supplied content entered into a web page and may be read by an attacker-controlled page or submitted when `submit` is true, so this is a `SINK`; `element`/`ref` select where the content goes. The extension implementation is not present, so exact browser behavior is undetermined.

browser_wait.rationale: `browser_wait` parses `time`, sends a wait command, and returns only a fixed status string containing the supplied time. It does not return browser/page content and has no call-time destination argument.
